title: MVNEX | Sebastian Sanchez
description: Case study for MVNEX, a C++ CLI that aims to give Maven an npm-like experience.
ogDescription: A C++ CLI for making Maven workflows feel simpler, faster, and more familiar.
name: MVNEX
headline: An npm-like experience for working with Maven with less friction.
summary: MVNEX is a CLI that aims to simplify everyday Maven work: easier-to-remember commands, more direct workflows, and a lighter experience for Java projects. It is built in C++ as an exercise in tooling, command design, and systems judgment.

problem.title: Starting point
problem.body: Maven is powerful, but its everyday experience can feel more verbose than modern tools like npm. MVNEX starts from that friction: create a simpler command layer for common tasks without losing control of the Java ecosystem.
points: Reduce repetitive commands in Maven projects.
Explore how a CLI can improve developer experience.
Build a small tool with systems fundamentals in C++.

role.title: My role
role.body: This is a personal project, so my role covers command design, C++ implementation, manual testing, internal decisions, and documenting the learning. The goal is for the tool to feel useful, not just technically interesting.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: MVNEX exists because there is a big difference between a tool that works and a tool that feels good in the terminal. The idea is to take npm's familiarity and apply it to common Maven tasks.
points: Make frequent commands easier to remember.
Reduce steps for repetitive build, test, and run workflows.
Learn to design tooling around real usage, not just implementation.

sections.title: What it explores
sections.body: The project explores command parsing, clear terminal interface design, process execution, and a simple internal architecture so the tool can grow over time.
points: Aliases and commands inspired by modern package manager experiences.
Running Maven tasks through a more direct interface.
Readable terminal messages oriented around action.
Work with Linux, Git, and manual testing cycles.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.body: The challenge is simplifying without hiding too much. MVNEX should feel lightweight and familiar while staying transparent about what it runs underneath.
points: Design commands that are easy to remember.
Keep mental compatibility with Maven instead of inventing another heavy tool.
Avoid premature abstractions while the usage flow is still maturing.
Document decisions so the project does not become a black box.

sections.title: What I want to learn
sections.body: I want to improve my judgment for designing developer tools: how to name commands, how to reduce friction, and how to build a CLI that feels fast and reliable.
points: Think more carefully about terminal user experience.
Write explicit C++ code that is easier to reason about.
Connect systems fundamentals with a usable tool.
Improve my instinct for knowing when a simple solution is already enough.

next.title: Next
next.body: Keep refining the command syntax, add clear usage examples, and better document which Maven tasks each command simplifies.
